goal_checks.notes: config.Config.SupabaseURL/SupabaseAnonKey present, env-overridable, default matches thinkboard-supabase local API port (54321).

auth.SupabaseClient.Login uses only net/http + encoding/json; POST {BaseURL}/auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with apikey header, confirmed against a live local GoTrue during manual smoke test (got a real 401).
Handler follows bind/call/map with no domain-state branching; 400 for binding failure, 401 for rejected credentials, 500 default path for network/5xx — verified by both unit tests and manual curl.
auth_test.go covers success, invalid-credentials, and bad-request without touching a live Supabase project.

cross_check_against_plan.section: §1 what the gateway does not own
cross_check_against_plan.result: Confirmed conflict: this endpoint is a password-flow proxy, which §1 assigns to client->Supabase directly. Not fixed silently — recorded in analyze.json.open_questions and in the response to the user as a follow-up decision (keep as dev-only vs. remove once apps/web exists).
Matches: AuthHandler.Login is exactly bind/call/map, three branches, no store access.
httpapi -> auth -> shared/errs only; no violation of the shared <- platform <- feature <- httpapi <- cmd direction.

issues_found: This login proxy duplicates a capability Supabase Auth already exposes directly to any client with the anon key — per §5.2's reuse rule ('if a new query duplicates something the client can already read through RLS/Supabase, it doesn't belong here'), this should likely be removed once apps/web talks to Supabase Auth directly instead of through the gateway.
